chapter: Cincinnati, Buffalo, Russell and Fletcher Henderson
title: Life in the Henderson band: lateness and drinking
summary: Henderson let the men arrive late; Coleman Hawkins led the lateness, and everyone drank.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: What did you get involved in, in that time? What was it like with the band?
Nothing but plain fun. We didn't do nothing but have a ball.
Can you describe some things that you did?
One thing, he was just a and he'd let you do like you want. He'd say he wanted you there at 8 o'clock. You'd get there about 9. Coleman Hawkins was a great one on that one. Nobody made time, nobody.
And he didn't make time because he called at my house.
Did that have an effect on the band working?

If Fletcher wanted you to start playing at 9 o'clock, he'll tell you about 7:30 or 8. Coleman Hawkins was always the leader on that one. He'd come in around about an hour late and then follow the leader, and we got used to it. If you didn't drink you weren't a member of the band.
You weren't a member of the band if you didn't drink?
You weren't a member of the band.
Is that when you started to drink?
Did you start to drink at that time with Fletcher?
Fletcher? Oh, brother! Yes sir, but you never see him
high when he's directing. He drank afterward.
